heroHeadline: Kast Prepares to Withdraw Security Reform as Budget Cuts Split His Coalition
heroSubtitle: President José Antonio Kast signalled on October 1 he will withdraw his constitutional security reform, which lacked Senate votes, and said on October 2 that doing so is 'no political defeat'; a cross-party text without the state of exception is being drafted. His 2027 budget, submitted September 30, cuts education programs and drew objections on October 3 from UDI deputies, who proposed trimming the INDH instead. Cadem put his approval at 36% (57% disapproval) on September 30, with unemployment now the second-biggest public concern.
footerNote: Data sourced from official Chilean government records (Biblioteca del Congreso, Banco Central, SERVEL), Rettig and Valech commissions, IACHR, CIPER Chile, and major international outlets.
